group.passage:
Imagine standing on a dazzling sea of white. There, the horizon [[1]] and it becomes hard to tell where the sky ends and the land begins. Welcome to Salar de Uyuni, located in southwest Bolivia, South America. Spanning over 10,500 square kilometers, it is the largest salt flat in the world. This [[2]] is so vast and flat that satellites use it to calibrate their instruments. Across the whole area, there is no more than a meter of [[3]] in elevation across its surface. The tiny “hills” and “valleys” are often just a few millimeters tall.
Salar de Uyuni has two distinct seasons. From December to April, which is the rainy season, [[4]] sheets of water cover the salt flat, transforming it into a stunning mirror that reflects the sky. This phenomenon occurs when nearby lakes overflow and spread water across the surface. The dry season lasts from May to November. Although the Salar’s famous mirror effect is rare during this time, visitors are [[5]] to another spectacular sight: polygon-shaped patterns covering the ground. As the salt dries out under the sun, it [[6]] and forms natural shapes that look like giant tiles. These patterns are usually hexagons and stretch as far as the eye can see. They are one of the most [[7]] features of Salar de Uyuni and make the salt flat look even more magical.
One of the most fascinating aspects of Salar de Uyuni is how it allows visitors to take playful, creative photos. Because the land is so flat and empty, clever optical illusions can be achieved through skillful [[8]] of props to create an interesting perspective effect. You can make it look like toy dinosaurs are chasing your friends, or like you’re climbing out of a giant peanut butter jar! The [[9]] is to put the camera very close to the prop and have your friends stand farther away. The closer the camera is to the prop, the bigger the prop will look [[10]] to the people in the frame. Just be careful—if the distance becomes too great, it can be hard to keep everything in focus.
In Salar de Uyuni, the endless white salt, the remarkable natural beauty, and the unique photography experiences combine to create a truly one-of-a-kind adventure.
